summary: Frontend changes largely remove the visible login gate and recipient-principal UI, and shift queries toward anonymous/public-mode usage. Backend shows reminders/profile functions no longer trapping on authorization, but the diff is truncated before message endpoints and some CRUD functions, so full REQ-9 coverage for messages (and possibly reminder delete) cannot be confirmed from the provided evidence.

missing_requirements.requirement: Remove or disable all login/logout and first-time profile setup UI flows (including the login button and profile setup dialog) so the interface reflects a shared/public mode.
missing_requirements.reason: The diff shows the header layout without login controls, but also indicates the LoginButton and ProfileSetupDialog components still exist. From the diff alone, it is not provable that these flows are fully removed/disabled everywhere or that all user-facing login-related text has been eliminated (only some public-mode wording is shown in updated messaging/reminder dialogs).

missing_requirements.requirement: Change backend authorization logic so anonymous callers can create/read/update/delete reminders and can send/read/delete messages without authorization traps.
missing_requirements.reason: backend/main.mo is truncated before showing message CRUD and at least one reminder operation is cut off ("Anyone can del..."), so it cannot be verified that all reminders CRUD and all message send/read/delete endpoints no longer enforce authorization or trap for anonymous callers.
evidence: backend/main.mo (truncated before delete reminder and message endpoints)

hallucinated_features.description: Backend profile-management endpoints explicitly described as guest-accessible (get/save caller profile; view any profile) even though the request only required making reminders/messages public.
hallucinated_features.reason: REQ-7/8/9/10 focus on removing authentication gating for reminders and messaging and removing profile setup prompts in the UI, but do not request changing backend profile authorization/visibility semantics.
